newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady, fuel oil up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil steady, fuel oil up.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afternoon on Friday but fuel oil firmed slightly supported by Chinese demand and expectations of buying from a local trader, market sources said.
"Fuel oil was supported steady Chinese demand and reduced supplies from Korea," one trader said.
He said bullish sentiment was aided by the absence of arbitrage cargoes due to high Gulf-East freight costs.
"The market is seeing strong buying from a local trader who is keeping prices up," another trader said.
January fuel oil swaps was last quoted at $119.25/$120.25 up from midday's $118.50/$119.75.
Gas oil swaps were largely unchanged this afternoon after a big increase in the morning.
January gas oil swaps were last traded at $30.90 up from this morning's trades at $30.50 and $30.75 a barrel, brokers said. The market was last quoted at $30.90/$31.00, they said.

Brokers said prices are expected to rise further in line with the stronger gas oil open on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) where January traded at $209.75 a tonne, up $4.50 from Thursday's close.
Jet fuel is well supported following recent large purchases from Japan and South Korea. A total of about 120,000-tonnes of spot jet/kerosene were sold this week to South Korea and Japan.
January jet fuel/gas oil swap spread or regrade was quoted at $1.60/$1.70 a barrel, brokers said.
Naphtha was quoted slightly weaker in quiet trade with January swaps at $23.10/$23.40 from Thursday's $23.30 offer.
